events.title: The fall of Granada
events.shortBlurb: The surrender of Granada to the Catholic Monarchs ended nearly eight centuries of Muslim rule in Spain…
body: On 2 January 1492 the city of Granada, the last Muslim kingdom on Iberian soil, surrendered to Ferdinand of Aragon and Isabella of Castile. Its Nasrid ruler, Muhammad XII, called Boabdil by the Christian chroniclers, handed over the keys of the Alhambra, and the Catholic Monarchs took possession of the city.

The surrender closed the Reconquista, the long recovery of Spain for Christendom that had stretched across nearly eight centuries since the Muslim conquest of 711. By the capitulations signed the previous November, the conquered were promised their property, their laws, and the free exercise of their religion.

The fall of Granada left the crowns of Castile and Aragon free of Muslim rule — only small Navarre still stood apart, until Ferdinand annexed it in 1512 — and freed the energies of its monarchs for the wider world; in the same year they dispatched Christopher Columbus across the Atlantic. The promised toleration did not long endure: within a decade the Muslims of Castile and Granada faced the choice of baptism or exile.
